title: The Letter of Valparaíso
premise: In 1904 Valparaíso, Rafael Sterling, a half-English apprentice clockmaker hiding his family's political past, is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock just as winter storms close the bridge and quarantine seals the port. Trapped among the observatory's eccentric staff, he discovers the clock conceals letters from his exiled father — and that the woman who hired him, Doña Inés, knows exactly who he is. When a ship offers one last berth before the tide, Rafael must decide whether to send his ailing half-sister to safety or claim escape for himself; in the end he gives her the berth, stays to wind the clock and face the truth of his name, and finds that the found family at the observatory becomes the home he was fleeing toward all along.
about_author: Yara Okafor is a former archivist who grew up between Lagos and Lisbon, where harbor cities taught her that every family keeps a locked drawer somewhere. She writes historical fiction about people whose survival depends on small, precise acts — much like clockwork.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Rafael arrives at the observatory under an assumed surname, POV his, and begins dismantling the master clock, finding a hidden compartment of unsent letters bearing his father's handwriting. He says nothing, keeping his hands busy as always. Emotional beat: wary curiosity curdling into dread as he realizes someone may have placed those letters for him to find.

chapters.title: What the Bridge Keeps Out
chapters.summary: The storm closes the bridge and quarantine locks the port; POV alternates between Rafael and Doña Inés, who quietly reveals she knew his father and has been protecting the letters for twenty years. The found family of astronomers, cooks, and clerks draws Rafael in despite himself. Emotional beat: the terror of being known warring with the first warmth of belonging.

chapters.title: One Berth on the Morning Tide
chapters.summary: A neutral merchant ship secures a single berth before sailing; Rafael learns his half-sister Lucía, weakened by fever, cannot survive another quarantined winter, while his own exposure as a Sterling could mean arrest if he stays. POV Rafael, with a devastating scene where Lucía begs him not to sacrifice himself again. Emotional beat: rising panic and guilt as the tide nears.

chapters.title: Wound and Set Right
chapters.summary: At dawn Rafael puts Lucía aboard, gives the guards his true name, and waits for arrest — but Doña Inés and the staff vouch for him, revealing the letters were testimony that clears his father's name at last. He winds the repaired master clock as the ship slips out. POV Rafael closing with Lucía's letter arriving by spring. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into peace; truth chosen over survival, and family found anyway.
